title: the dress that came back

opening.dialogue: A life is a sending; the last rai is where the soi keeps what it has not yet decided to send. Je Fah stands at the edge of the unbuilt field with a dress over her arm, and the dress is the color of a bus she finally boarded at fifty-eight.
The resident from 1208 says this is hers. She donated it to the wat flood drive last year. Now it's on my rack with a price tag and a ring light waiting.
I washed it at Saduek Sak. The whole bench watched it spin. Nobody said a word until tonight.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She holds the dress up against the field light and lets the hem drop toward the dirt.
turns.dialogue: You'll regret walking away from this one, Lek. The soi already thinks my charity was a costume. If I give it back now, they'll say I only did it because I got caught.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She taps the phone mount twice, hard, and the ring light flickers on her face.
turns.dialogue: The resident means it. She's not asking for the dress back — she's asking what I am. And she's serious enough to say it in front of the bench.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She sets the tea glass down on the chalk board and draws a circle around two names.
turns.dialogue: We live near each other, her and me. Same soi, same bench, same machines. That's what makes it worse — she didn't have to look far to find the dress.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She turns the QR sign toward Lek and taps the payment code with one nail.
turns.dialogue: Can you follow what the soi is saying? They think I bought the dress off a donation pile. They think the whole flood drive was stock intake.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She looks at the phone mount, thumb hovering, then drops her hand.
turns.dialogue: I called the wat office to check the donation ledger. He hung up on me. Said the flood drive books were already closed.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She folds the dress over the chalk board and looks at the field instead of Lek.
turns.dialogue: I don't feel the same about the live tonight. It used to be a rack and a ring light. Now it's a woman's dress and a bench that watched it spin.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She lifts both hands off the tea glass and lets them fall against her thighs.
turns.dialogue: I don't understand anything. Was it a donation or was it stock? I signed for a bag at the wat, and now the bag is a rack, and the rack is a live.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She pulls Lek behind the deed bag leaning against the field marker.
turns.dialogue: Don't let her see you looking at the dress. The resident from 1208 is at the soi mouth, and she's walking this way.

je_fah_turn_1.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_1.line: She turns the chalk board so the price column faces the field. 'If I give it back, I'm admitting the whole rack was a costume.'

je_fah_turn_2.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_2.line: The ring light steadies. 'She means it, Lek. She's not asking for a refund — she's asking what I am.'

je_fah_turn_3.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_3.line: She circles the two names twice. 'We live near each other. That's the whole problem.'

je_fah_turn_4.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_4.line: She flips the QR sign face-down. 'Can you follow? They think the flood drive was my supplier.'

je_fah_turn_5.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_5.line: She sets the phone mount on the deed bag. 'The wat office hung up. The books are closed. I have a dress and no paper.'
je_fah_turn_5.bubble: Je Fah has no donation receipt

je_fah_turn_6.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_6.line: She folds the dress smaller than it needs to be. 'I don't feel the same about the live tonight.'

je_fah_turn_7.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_7.line: She picks up the tea glass and sets it down without drinking. 'I don't understand anything. Donation or stock — I signed for a bag and now it's a rack.'

je_fah_turn_8.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_8.line: She pulls Lek behind the deed bag. 'Don't let her see you. The resident is walking this way, and she's carrying something.'

finale.dialogue: She hangs the dress on the field marker, not the rack. 'Let the soi see it out here first. A dress that came back has to stand in the light before it goes anywhere.'
The ring light goes off. The dress stays on the marker, and the last rai holds it the way a stop holds a village waiting at a stop the bus no longer serves.

obj_biscuit_tin.name: the biscuit tin of ledgers
obj_biscuit_tin.description: Biscuit tin, lid bent from a decade of thumbs, three vendors' books sorted by which soi they belong to.

obj_word_notebook.name: the word notebook
obj_word_notebook.description: Pocket notebook, cover soft from handling, pages filled with other people's words in Lek's small hand.

obj_stamp_keys.name: the stamp-drawer keys
obj_stamp_keys.description: Two brass keys on a wire ring, warm from his pocket, one notched from the time he dropped them at the win rank.

obj_qr_sign.name: the QR sign
obj_qr_sign.description: Laminated card, corners curled from the heat, payment code printed over a photo of a rack of clothes.

obj_deed_bag.name: the deed in the rice bag
obj_deed_bag.description: Rice bag, stitched shut with fishing line, a folded deed inside that names the last rai and three people who no longer come to collect.

obj_chalk_board.name: the queue board
obj_chalk_board.description: Chalk board, frame warped from rain, tonight's rack list written in Je Fah's quick hand with two names circled.

obj_share_envelope.name: the circle envelope
obj_share_envelope.description: Manila envelope, flap soft from opening, Mae Tim's share-circle payout inside with one member's name penciled in the corner.

obj_phone_mount.name: the phone mount
obj_phone_mount.description: Clamp mount, spring tired, holds a phone at the exact angle that makes a dress look like it is floating.

obj_tea_glass.name: the tea-stall glass
obj_tea_glass.description: Small glass, rim chipped, sweet tea gone warm and skinned over on the field marker.

outcomeRules.speaker: char_je_fah
outcomeRules.line: She opens the tin and reads the ledgers upside down, correctly. 'The wat donation is here — a bag signed for, no item list. That's the hole the dress fell through.'
outcomeRules.bubble: Je Fah has seen the donation entry

outcomeRules.speaker: char_je_fah
outcomeRules.line: She writes the resident's name in Lek's notebook and under it: 'dress returned to the rack, not the wat.' 'Now the soi can read it before the live does.'
outcomeRules.bubble: The dress will be returned on the record

char_je_fah: She turns the {item} over once and sets it back on the field marker. 'Not tonight, Lek. The soi is already talking.'
She taps the {item} against the chalk board. 'The wat donation is the hole here. Show me something with a date on it.'
She holds the {item} up to the ring light. 'The dress came from a bag with no item list. Bring me the ledger that says so, and I'll put my name under it.'
narrator: The {item} goes back into the night with nothing settled. The dress hangs on the marker; the soi waits.
Nothing comes of the {item} yet. Je Fah watches the soi mouth the way the bench watches a machine spin.
Je Fah's gaze flicks from the {item} to the dress on the marker and back — a route mapped, a record missing.
